Sean —

Thanks for the context. Below are two draft clause options (clean text) you can send to Stratus. I kept the operational items explicit to reduce back-and-forth.

Option A (Customer-forward):
"Termination for Convenience: Either party may terminate the Agreement for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the other party. If Redwood terminates for convenience, Redwood shall refund any pre-paid but unused fees. If Customer terminates for convenience, Customer's sole liability shall be limited to payment of fees equal to six (6) months of Customer's average monthly fees during the preceding three (3) months. In all cases, Redwood will provide a transition package consisting of: (i) export of customer data and logs within ten (10) business days of termination; (ii) KV cache snapshot available for secure download for thirty (30) days; and (iii) up to thirty (30) days of remote transition support at standard rates."
Option B (Balanced):
"Termination for Convenience: Either party may terminate the Agreement for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice. If Customer terminates for convenience, Customer's liability shall be limited to payment of fees equal to three (3) months of Customer's average monthly fees during the preceding three (3) months, plus pro-rated charges for any committed but unused dedicated capacity. Redwood will provide a transition package consisting of: (i) export of customer data and logs within ten (10) business days; (ii) KV cache snapshot available for secure download for thirty (30) days; and (iii) up to thirty (30) days of remote transition support at Redwood's then-current professional services hourly rates."
Comments / recommendation: present Option B first — it retains a reasonable cap while offering concrete transition actions (exports + 30 days support) that procurement asked for. If Stratus pushes back, be prepared to move to Option A but ask for an expanded TCV or one-time onboarding recovery fee.

Other items: confirm the auto-renew notice email addresses (procurement@stratushealth.com + legal@stratushealth.com) and add an explicit obligation that Redwood will send automated renewal reminders at least 75 days before renewal to those aliases. That gives both teams time to act within the 60-day window.

I'll draft a short redline for the order form with Option B inserted and send to you by EOD; please loop Olivia and procurement.

—Marissa
